world.name: Port Averill
world.premise: A harbor town on the Michigan shore of Lake Huron, 1900 onward. Real calendar and climate, invented town, people, and ships. The lake is the world's one large fact: it sets the work, the weather, the money, and who comes home.
time_rules: All time is an integer count of minutes since the world epoch.
Local mean time. No daylight saving, no leap seconds, so every day is exactly 1440 minutes.
Seasons are meteorological: winter is December through February and is named for the year it begins in.

places.name: Port Averill, Michigan
places.note: Fictional. Population about 4,100 in 1941. Ferry slip, coal dock, a cannery, one high school.

places.name: Sable Bank
places.note: Fictional shoal eleven miles offshore, badly charted until Nell charts it.

places.name: Sable Point Light
places.note: Fictional lighthouse at the north end of the harbor.

places.name: Detroit, Michigan
places.note: Home of the Great Lakes Survey Office, a fictional agency.

people.name: Laszlo Varga

people.name: Tomas Varga
people.relation: brother; lost on the Ellen Tarn

people.name: Martin Halloran
people.relation: chief of the survey launch; first to let her aboard

month_motif.01: The harbor is locked. People walk on the lake and argue about how thick the ice is.
month_motif.02: The coldest and longest month. Ice shanties, coal bills, cabin fever.
month_motif.03: The ice groans. Everyone is waiting and pretending not to be.
month_motif.04: Breakup. The first boat through the channel is the town's real new year.
month_motif.05: Fitting-out. Paint, tar, and the survey and ferry crews signing on.
month_motif.06: Long light. School ends, the cannery hires, the water is still dangerously cold.
month_motif.07: Summer people arrive on the ferry and the town makes its money.
month_motif.08: Warm water at last, thunderheads over the bank, the best charting weather.
month_motif.09: Summer people leave. School, north wind, and the first honest cold night.
month_motif.10: Last good weeks on the water. Boats are hurried; decisions get made.
month_motif.11: The gale month. Nobody in Port Averill schedules anything important on the lake.
month_motif.12: Boats laid up. Ice skim in the slip. The town turns indoors.

season_focus.spring: Sleep and milk in a house that smells of coal.
season_focus.summer: Carried to the slip to see the boats.
season_focus.winter: Wrapped by the stove while the harbor freezes.

season_focus.spring: Mud, the slip, and pointing at every boat.
season_focus.summer: Bare feet on the breakwater, one hand held.
season_focus.fall: New words, most of them about boats.
season_focus.winter: Underfoot in a small warm kitchen.

season_focus.spring: Waiting for breakup, then watching it from the schoolroom.
season_focus.summer: No school; the harbor all day.
season_focus.fall: New grade, cold mornings, chores before school.
season_focus.winter: Skating, coal, and reading by the stove.

season_focus.spring: First steps in the brace, on the kitchen floor.
season_focus.summer: The window, the boats she can see, and the ones she can't.
season_focus.fall: Hot packs and arithmetic brought home by Mrs. Dunn.
season_focus.winter: A long indoor winter with the charts spread on the bed.

season_focus.spring: Exams and the harbor office after school.
season_focus.summer: Full days copying manifests, reading every chart in the building.
season_focus.fall: Mrs. Dunn's problem sets and the walk home along the breakwater.
season_focus.winter: Boats laid up, office quiet, the calculus book open under the ledger.

season_focus.spring: Finals, and a lake she can't see from Ann Arbor.
season_focus.summer: A department job running tables, and a lake she can only visit.
season_focus.fall: New courses; the only woman in most of the rooms.
season_focus.winter: Long nights at the carrel and a radiator that bangs.

season_focus.spring: The launches fitting out without her.
season_focus.summer: Reducing other people's soundings in a hot office.
season_focus.fall: Field books arrive; she finds their errors.
season_focus.winter: All hands on data reduction; she is the fastest they have.

season_focus.spring: Fitting out the launch and planning lines.
season_focus.summer: Sounding from first light; sleeping in port towns.
season_focus.fall: Racing the gales to finish the lines.
season_focus.winter: Back in Detroit, turning field books into charts.

season_focus.spring: Planning lines she will run for only part of the season.
season_focus.summer: Field weeks, phone calls home, guilt in both directions.
season_focus.fall: School shoes, field books, and the office again.
season_focus.winter: Charts by day, children by evening, the Sable Bank file by night.

season_focus.spring: Breakup watched from her own window; drafting table by the east light.
season_focus.summer: A rented launch, the bank, and whatever funding covered.
season_focus.fall: Inking the season's lines before the gales.
season_focus.winter: The long drafting months; the town's questions at the post office.

season_focus.spring: Breakup again; she still logs the date.
season_focus.summer: Grandchildren on the breakwater, chart lessons on the porch.
season_focus.fall: The last good walks before the leg stiffens with the cold.
season_focus.winter: Archive boxes, radio, and the long view of the ice.

season_focus.spring: Ada reads her the ice-out date; she corrects the source.
season_focus.summer: A chair on the porch where she can see the slip.
season_focus.fall: Fewer walks. She watches the water get its color back.
season_focus.winter: The stove, the radio, naps that run together.

residence.value: a flat off Jefferson Avenue, Detroit
a house on Burns Avenue, Detroit
her mother's house, Harbor Street, Port Averill

life.story: Nell Varga was born during breakup on Lake Huron and wanted to run her father's ferry. Polio and the rules of the time closed that door. Her brother's ship went down when she was sixteen, and no one could say where, because no one had properly charted that water. So she learned mathematics, talked her way onto a survey launch, raised two children between field seasons, came home to nurse her mother, and spent thirty-nine years making the chart that finally found him. She lived long enough to teach a town's children to read it.

segments.name: Infancy
segments.developmental_task: Learn whether the world can be trusted.
segments.summary: Born during breakup. Her father ships out with the merchant fleet when she is eighteen months old; the house narrows to Ruth, Tomas, and the stove.

statements.text: She is held, fed, and answered, mostly by the same two people.
A man who was in the house is no longer in the house. She cannot know this as a fact, only as a change.

segments.name: Early Childhood
segments.developmental_task: Become a separate person with a will and a language.
segments.summary: A stranger comes home from the war and turns out to be her father. She wins him over by asking what the numbers on the chart mean.

statements.text: I want to know what the numbers in the water mean.
The man in the kitchen is my father and I am supposed to like him.

segments.name: Middle Childhood
segments.developmental_task: Become good at something, and find out what you are allowed to be.
segments.summary: She memorizes the harbor and decides to be a ferry pilot. At eleven, polio takes the strength of her left leg in the summer's last epidemic, and the plan with it.

statements.text: I am going to run the Averill ferry.
My left leg is not going to do what it did.
I will walk into that school on my own.

segments.name: Adolescence
segments.developmental_task: Work out who you are when the first answer is gone.
segments.summary: Mathematics, under Mrs. Dunn, replaces the wheel. Tomas is lost with the Ellen Tarn in November 1957, and the official position of the wreck is a guess. She leaves on a scholarship with a reason.

statements.text: I am better at this than anyone in the building, and the building knows it.
I have to get out of this town while I can still be someone other than the girl with the brace.
Nobody knows where Tomas is because nobody ever charted that water. Someone could.

segments.name: Emerging Adulthood
segments.developmental_task: Test the self against the world and choose what to commit to.
segments.summary: A mathematics degree, then the back room of the Great Lakes Survey reducing other people's soundings. She is told the launch is no place for a woman with a brace, finds enough errors to change that, and meets Emeka Obi at an argument about a bridge.

statements.text: I will take my own soundings.
Every chart is an argument, and most of them have not been checked.
This is a man who will argue with me until we are both right.

segments.name: Early Adulthood
segments.developmental_task: Build things that outlast your own wants: work, family, a household.
segments.summary: Ada and Daniel are born. She cuts her field seasons in half and never quite forgives either side of the trade. The Sable Bank file grows at night. Her father dies. Her mother begins to forget.

statements.text: I can have the water and the children if I never sleep.
Every season I took, they were smaller when I got back.
The Sable Bank chart is the real work. Everything else pays for it.

segments.name: Midlife
segments.developmental_task: Give back what you have built, and repair what the building cost.
segments.summary: She moves home to nurse Ruth, publishes the Sable Bank chart in 1989, and in July 1996, working from her own contours, finds the Ellen Tarn in 41 fathoms, nine miles from the official position.

statements.text: She taught me to read. I can help her find the kitchen.
It is correct. I have checked it for eleven years and it is correct.
He is at 41 fathoms. I know where he is now.

segments.name: Late Adulthood
segments.developmental_task: Make meaning of the whole and pass it on.
segments.summary: She retires, gives the archive to the town, and teaches local children to read a chart on Tuesdays and Thursdays. Emeka dies in 2012. Post-polio weakness returns to the leg.

statements.text: Any kid in this town ought to be able to look at the water and know what's under it.
I keep saving arguments for him.

segments.name: Final Years
segments.developmental_task: Accept dependence, finish what can be finished, let the rest go.
segments.summary: A fall on the ice ends living alone. Ada moves in. Ife takes over the Tuesday lessons. Nell dies at dawn in October, in the house she was born in, with the slip in view.

statements.text: Ada is holding my arm the way I held Mother's. Fine.
It's charted. Somebody else can check it now.

plans.text: Learn the numbers on the chart well enough to read depths to Papa before school starts.

milestones.text: Read a depth aloud off the harbor chart

plans.text: Run the Averill ferry by twenty-one: every buoy by ten, the wheel by eleven, deckhand at sixteen.

milestones.text: Name every buoy and light from memory
Take the wheel with Papa standing by

plans.text: Walk into school with the brace and no help by the fall term.
Win the state scholarship and leave for Ann Arbor.

milestones.text: Finish the calculus book with Mrs. Dunn

plans.text: Learn how charts are made, then get someone with a boat to look for the Ellen Tarn.
No one is coming to look. Run the Sable Bank lines myself during survey seasons and search it by 1980.

milestones.text: Finish a complete line set over the northern bank

plans.text: Finish the chart first. The contours will show where a ship that broke up on that shoal would have come to rest. Then search there.
Find enough errors in the field books that Halloran has to bring me out to see how they happen.

milestones.text: Catch a material error in a published sheet
Get a berth on the launch

plans.text: Three field months while the baby is small, then back to full seasons when the baby starts school.
Stop waiting for full seasons. Three months a year is the job. Be home by supper the other nine.
Turn the Sable Bank file into a publishable chart, on my own time if I must.
Leave the Survey, sell Burns Avenue, and move home before Mother can't be left alone.
Give the field books and drafts to the town library, indexed, before my memory is part of the index.

milestones.text: Hand the archive to the library

plans.text: Teach every local kid who shows up to read a chart. Two afternoons a week, for as long as the leg allows.
Hand Ife the lessons and the corrections file. Say the plain things to Ada and Daniel while I still can.

events.title: Born during breakup
events.text: Born at home on Harbor Street at 4:12 in the morning while the ice goes out of the harbor. The midwife remarks on the noise.

events.title: Laszlo ships out
events.text: Her father leaves for the merchant fleet. She is carried to the depot and sleeps through it.

events.title: A stranger comes home
events.text: Laszlo walks up Harbor Street with a duffel bag. Nell, four, hides behind Ruth and will not come out for him.

events.title: What do the numbers mean?
events.text: He has the harbor chart on the kitchen table. She climbs up and asks about the numbers in the water. It is the first thing she has ever said to him on purpose.

events.title: Reads a depth aloud
events.text: On the ferry deck, she reads a depth off the harbor chart to her father, and it's right.

events.title: First day of school
events.text: Mrs. Lund's room, the desk by the window, the harbor in view.

events.title: Announces the plan
events.text: At supper she tells the family she is going to run the ferry. Tomas laughs. Laszlo doesn't.

events.title: Names every buoy
events.text: Laszlo tests her from the slip to Sable Point. She misses none.

events.title: Takes the wheel
events.text: An empty early crossing. Her father stands behind her and doesn't touch anything for twenty minutes.

events.title: Polio
events.text: Headache at the beach, a stiff neck by noon, the ambulance to Saginaw by afternoon. She will not stand again for six months.

events.title: Crosses the kitchen
events.text: Stove to table in the brace, alone, while Ruth pretends to look at something else.

events.title: Walks into school
events.text: It takes eleven minutes from the door to her desk. Nobody helps, because she told them she would never forgive it.

events.title: Mrs. Dunn keeps her after class
events.text: A geometry proof done by a method not in the book. Mrs. Dunn slides a calculus text across the desk and says to bring it back when it's finished.

events.title: Hired at the harbor office
events.text: Ruth gets her work copying manifests. It puts every chart in the building within reach.

events.title: The Ellen Tarn is overdue
events.text: The freighter Ellen Tarn stops answering in a gale north of the bank with Tomas, nineteen, among the crew of twenty-three. Ruth takes the call at the harbor office and doesn't take off her coat all night.

events.title: The official position
events.text: She reads the inquiry notice at the office and looks up its position on the chart. The soundings there are sixty-year-old lead lines with blank water between them. It's a guess. She begins a file.

events.title: Returns the calculus book
events.text: Mrs. Dunn looks through the worked problems and hands her a harder book.

events.title: The state scholarship
events.text: The letter arrives at the harbor office, because that is where she had told them to send it.

events.title: Leaves Port Averill
events.text: The morning bus. Laszlo carries the suitcase; Ruth checks the leg brace strap one more time.

events.title: Takes her degree
events.text: Mathematics with honors. Laszlo wears the suit from his wedding.

events.title: Hired by the Survey
events.text: A desk in the Detroit back room, reducing soundings. She asks about going out on the launch and is told, kindly, no.

events.title: Finds the error
events.text: A systematic tide-gauge error across a published sheet of Saginaw Bay. Halloran reads her note twice, then walks to her desk.

events.title: Argument about a bridge
events.text: At an engineering society lecture she tells a stranger his scour estimates are wrong. Emeka Obi tells her why they aren't. They are still arguing when the hall closes.

events.title: Aboard the launch
events.text: Halloran says the launch has a ladder and it's her problem. She gets up the ladder. She takes her first sounding at 6:31.

events.title: Marries Emeka
events.text: A courthouse in Detroit, a loud dinner afterward. Not everyone in either family attends. The ones who do stay late.

events.title: Ada is born
events.text: Ruth Adaeze Obi, named for both grandmothers' sides of the argument.

events.title: Daniel is born
events.text: Daniel Tomas Obi. She says the middle name aloud for the first time in years.

events.title: The first day she misses
events.text: Ada starts first grade while Nell is on a launch off Alpena. She reads about it in a letter. That night she rewrites the plan.

events.title: The northern lines close
events.text: The last line over the north Sable Bank. For the first time, the file holds enough to draw.

events.title: Laszlo dies
events.text: A heart attack in the night, in the coldest week of the year. The ferry crew carry him across the ice to the cemetery road.

events.title: Ruth can't find the kitchen
events.text: On a visit home, Ruth, who had kept the harbor's books for thirty years, stands in the hallway of her own house and asks where the kitchen went.

events.title: Moves back to Harbor Street
events.text: Emeka takes a county job. Ada, fourteen, does not forgive the move until Christmas. Nell sets her drafting table by the east window.

events.title: The Sable Bank chart is published
events.text: Sheet 14866, compiled by E. Varga Obi. Two shoals moved. One shipping advisory reissued. No one says anything at the post office except old Peterson, who says it's about time.

events.title: Ruth dies
events.text: In the house, in the last week of the ice. At the end she calls Nell by Tomas's name. Nell answers.

events.title: Ife is born
events.text: Ada's daughter, in Minneapolis. Nell drives there alone, seven hundred miles with the bad leg, and won't discuss it.

events.title: Finds the Ellen Tarn
events.text: From a rented launch, working from her own contours. The sonar trace rises at 41 fathoms, nine miles from the official position, just where a hull driven off the shoal would have come to rest. She logs the position. Then she shuts the engine off and sits.

events.title: The names, with a position
events.text: The fortieth anniversary service. For the first time, the plaque has coordinates. Twenty-three names.

events.title: Puts down the pen
events.text: She inks the last correction on the Sable sheet, caps the pen, and walks to the breakwater.

events.title: Archive goes to the library
events.text: One hundred and twelve boxes, indexed by hand.

events.title: First chart class
events.text: Four children and one reluctant father on the library floor. She asks them what the numbers in the water mean.

events.title: Emeka dies
events.text: After a short illness. He had disputed the doctor's figures until the Tuesday before.

events.title: The leg again
events.text: A neurologist in Saginaw, the same hospital, gives it a name: post-polio syndrome. She asks for the numbers.

events.title: The fall on the ice
events.text: On the breakwater steps. A broken hip and two hours in the cold before a dog walker sees her. Ada moves home within the month.

events.title: Ife runs the lesson
events.text: On the porch, in masks. Ife, nineteen, teaches it, and Nell corrects only one bearing.

events.title: Hands over the corrections file
events.text: Fifty-seven years of notes on what's still wrong with the chart. "It's not finished," she says. "That's the point of it."

events.title: Dies at first light
events.text: In the house on Harbor Street, the slip in view, the north wind up. Ada is in the room. The ferry's first crossing is at 6:40.
